readings.title: The photograph with an uncertain date
readings.instruction: Read the passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A local archive received a photograph of a crowded market. The donor believed it was taken in the early 1960s, but no date appeared on the back. A shop sign in the image suggested it might be slightly later. Rather than choose one date without evidence, the archivist recorded both the donor's memory and the clue from the sign. The catalogue described the date as approximate. Months later, another resident identified a stallholder and supplied a dated receipt from the same event. The record could then be refined without hiding how the earlier estimate had been reached.
knowledgePoints: 阅读理解：篇章结构与信息判断

readings.title: A guide who stopped speaking first
readings.instruction: Read the passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: During neighbourhood tours, guide Elena once explained every street before allowing questions. Visitors listened politely but rarely joined in. She changed the opening of each stop by asking what people noticed. One visitor pointed to marks above a doorway; another asked why several houses shared a courtyard. These observations led naturally into the area's history. Elena still prepared accurate information and corrected misunderstandings, but she no longer assumed that silence meant interest. The tours became more conversational. Visitors often remembered details connected to their own questions more clearly than facts delivered in a long introduction.
knowledgePoints: 阅读理解：篇章结构与信息判断

readings.title: An exhibition written for neighbours
readings.instruction: Read the passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A small history exhibition used technical language borrowed from an academic report. Local residents recognised the objects but struggled with the labels. The curator invited a reading group to discuss a sample label. Members did not ask for the history to be simplified into a cheerful story. They wanted shorter sentences, explanations of unfamiliar terms and a clear connection between each object and local life. The curator revised the labels while keeping difficult facts. A former factory worker then contributed a brief personal account. The exhibition became easier to enter intellectually without pretending that the town's past had been uncomplicated.
knowledgePoints: 阅读理解：篇章结构与信息判断

readings.title: Keeping two versions of a festival story
readings.instruction: Read the passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: Two older residents told different stories about why their village held an autumn lantern walk. One linked it to the end of field work; the other remembered it as a children's activity introduced by a teacher. The festival committee initially wanted one official explanation for its leaflet. After discussion, it printed both accounts, clearly attributed to their speakers, and invited further memories. This approach did not establish which story was historically earliest. It showed how the event had acquired different meanings for different people. The leaflet became an invitation to conversation as well as a guide to the evening's programme.
knowledgePoints: 阅读理解：篇章结构与信息判断

translation.stem:
Translate the following passage into Chinese:
Public history becomes richer when people can see where an account comes from. A photograph, a written record and a personal memory may each reveal a different part of an event. They do not always agree. Recording those differences openly allows later readers to ask better questions. An honest explanation of uncertainty can be more valuable than a confident story built on weak evidence.
knowledgePoints: 英译汉：语义准确与中文表达
translation.explanation: 准确处理where宾语从句、each的分配意义以及最后的比较。
translation.referenceAnswer: 当人们能够看到一段叙述的来源时，公共历史就会更加丰富。照片、书面记录和个人记忆可能各自揭示一个事件的不同侧面。它们并不总是一致。公开记录这些差异，可以让后来的读者提出更有价值的问题。诚实地说明不确定性，可能比建立在薄弱证据上的自信叙述更有价值。

writing.stem: Write 100–150 words in English inviting residents to contribute to a local memory project. Explain the kinds of material wanted, how contributors will retain control over personal material, and how to take part.
knowledgePoints: 写作：任务完成、组织与语言
writing.explanation: 涵盖征集范围、材料与受访者控制权及参与渠道。
writing.sampleAnswer:
Our community archive is collecting memories of everyday life around the old market. We welcome photographs, short written accounts and recorded conversations about shops, work and local celebrations. You do not need to know an exact date; please simply tell us what you remember and what remains uncertain.
Original photographs can be scanned and returned. Before any personal account is displayed, we will explain its intended use and ask for permission. Interview participants may skip questions and will have an opportunity to comment on the transcript.
To take part, contact the library desk or attend our collection afternoon next Saturday. Your contribution may help neighbours understand places they pass every day and preserve details that are missing from official records.

criteria.name: 组织连贯
criteria.description: 段落清晰，衔接自然，有合适的开头和结尾。
